summary: In Greek mythology, Alastor is a Pylian warrior whom Nestor arrays beside Pelagon, Chromius, Haemon, and Bias when Agamemnon reviews the host. Wikipedia's Alastor article also attaches to this Pylian the later scenes in which Alastor and Mecisteus carry wounded Teucer and Hypsenor from the field — scenes the atlas stages on the separate node alastor-achaean.

sections.heading: In Nestor's line
paragraphs: In Iliad 4 Nestor draws up mighty Pelagon, Alastor, Chromius, lord Haemon, and Bias shepherd of the host — charioteers before the footmen — when Agamemnon comes among the Pylians.

Some handbook traditions identify this arrayed Pylian with the Alastor who later bears the wounded beside Mecisteus; the atlas keeps alastor-pylian (Catalogue/array) and alastor-achaean (bearer) as separate nodes while sharing the Wikipedia page.

sections.heading: Homonym care
paragraphs: The atlas id alastor-pylian is Nestor's arrayed Pylian alone. Distinct from alastor-achaean, alastor-lycian, alastor-trojan, and the Neleid prince Alastor son of Neleus slain by Heracles.
